structural_deadlock_diagnosis.summary: exp2810 was designated as 'Phase B Pre-Test Cascade Fix v4'. Its prompt declared three fixes: (1) mock PySAT in test_experiment_1504_thrml_carnot_simulator_parity_v3.py, (2) create hardware/kv260/discrete_sb_256_tb.v Verilog stub, (3) repair test_docs.py::test_public_docs_cover_latest_pbt_and_fpga_reporting. Each fix individually is a 1-2 file edit. BUT the conductor's research_step() runs a pre-test gate BEFORE handing any task to the agent. If the pre-test gate fails, the task is SKIP'd before the agent ever sees the prompt. So exp2810 cannot fix the cascade because the cascade prevents exp2810 from launching. After 3 consecutive SKIPs the conductor retired exp2810 as a merit-failure, which then cascade-blocked exp2811-2814/2816/2817 via the gated_on chain. This is the third consecutive milestone (.263, .264, .265 also showed variants) where a 'fix the pre-test cascade' task has been queued and failed the same way.
structural_deadlock_diagnosis.root_cause_class: self-referential-gate (conductor's safety mechanism prevents the only task that could disable that safety mechanism)

structural_deadlock_diagnosis.operator_resolution_path: The fix CANNOT be inside the conductor. It must be either (a) outer-loop Claude/operator runs the three test fixes directly in the working tree and commits, OR (b) scripts/research_conductor.py is modified to allow a 'bootstrap' class of task that bypasses the pre-test gate, OR (c) the offending tests are quarantined out of the conductor's pre-test subset until the proper fixes land. Option (a) is the cleanest because per CLAUDE.md the conductor itself must not be modified mid-task ('Do NOT modify scripts/research_conductor.py').
